qualification_rule: Only papers that explicitly assign two or more depot-to-depot delivery trips to the same physical vehicle within one workday, planning horizon, or period are included.

records.paper: Brandão, J.; Mercer, A. (1998), The multi-trip vehicle routing problem, Journal of the Operational Research Society 49:799-805
records.source_type: author-uploaded full text; page references below use the page numbers printed in that full text
records.multitrip_evidence: p.2 states that the practical algorithm allowed any number of multiple trips per day. p.4 defines a tour as a set of routes assigned to the same vehicle, h_v as the number of routes assigned to vehicle v, and sums route times over that vehicle.
records.fleet_size_given_or_endogenous: BOTH. Total vehicles V may be defined a priori or determined by the algorithm (p.4). In the benchmark comparison, each selected V is fixed for that subproblem (p.13).
records.how_total_derived: No demand/capacity formula for V. The benchmarks enumerate integer V from 1 to V_max; workday limits are then T1=round(1.05 Z*/V) and T2=round(1.10 Z*/V), where Z* is a quasi-optimal unrestricted-VRP travel value (p.13).
records.total_shrinks_or_fixed: Fixed within each theoretical subproblem. Separately, the p.2 practical example cited by the authors reports that allowing a second trip reduced required vehicles from 21 to 19; no universal shrink factor is proposed.
records.max_trips_per_vehicle: No numerical cap. The practical algorithm allows any number per day, bounded by delivery windows and legal driver schedules (p.2); the simplified model uses maximum driving time and overtime (p.4).
records.benefit_reported_as: The introduction cites an empirical 21-to-19 vehicle reduction and 5% lower unit delivery cost (p.2). The simplified benchmark reports total travel time and balance of daily vehicle tours, not a single-trip causal comparison (pp.13-16).
records.fixed_cost_billing_unit: The simplified TSMTVRP has no vehicle fixed-cost term and minimizes travel time for a given V (pp.3-4). The practical narrative lists driver, fuel, fleet-maintenance and hired-vehicle costs, but does not give an algebraic billing unit (p.2).

records.paper: Cattaruzza, D.; Absi, N.; Feillet, D.; Vidal, T. (2014), A memetic algorithm for the Multi Trip Vehicle Routing Problem, European Journal of Operational Research 236:833-848
records.source_type: author manuscript; page references below use the manuscript's printed pages
records.multitrip_evidence: p.1 states that each physical vehicle can perform several trips during the working day, return to the depot, reload, and start another service trip. It defines a depot fleet of m vehicles and limits the sum of route durations assigned to one vehicle by T_H.
records.fleet_size_given_or_endogenous: GIVEN. m is an instance input.
records.how_total_derived: No formula derives m from total demand or capacity. The benchmark scans different m and sets T_H1=round(1.05 z*/m), T_H2=round(1.10 z*/m), where z* is the original CVRP solution value (p.13).
records.total_shrinks_or_fixed: Fixed within each instance; routes are packed into the given m vehicles. The paper does not automatically shrink m when multi-trip is enabled (pp.1,13).
records.max_trips_per_vehicle: No numerical cap. The only aggregate restriction is that total duration of routes assigned to a vehicle cannot exceed T_H (p.1).
records.benefit_reported_as: Total travel time, feasibility rate, and algorithmic solution quality on multi-trip benchmarks (pp.15-23); no isolated single-trip versus multi-trip benefit.
records.fixed_cost_billing_unit: NONE. The objective is total travel time (p.1).

records.paper: Zhen, L.; Ma, C.; Wang, K.; Xiao, L.; Zhang, W. (2020), Multi-depot multi-trip vehicle routing problem with time windows and release dates, Transportation Research Part E 135:101866
records.multitrip_evidence: p.3 says each depot owns a fleet, each trip starts and ends at the same depot, and trips of the same vehicle cannot overlap. p.4 indexes vehicle k and trip w and gives real trip sets such as {1,2,3}. p.17 illustrates k0 performing two depot-customer-depot trips.
records.fleet_size_given_or_endogenous: GIVEN. K and W are input sets; objective (1) minimizes travel time and does not purchase vehicles (pp.3-4).
records.how_total_derived: The instance identifier directly encodes customers, depots, total vehicles, and maximum trips per vehicle (p.13). No demand, capacity, time-window, or horizon formula is supplied. A frequent two-vehicles-per-depot pattern is observable in the tables but is not justified as a derivation.
records.total_shrinks_or_fixed: Fixed within each instance. Table 5 varies vehicle totals as sensitivity scenarios, not as an automatic consequence of enabling multi-trip (pp.13-14).
records.max_trips_per_vehicle: 3 for the small and 10-80 customer main instances; 5 for 90-200 customer main instances (pp.12-13); 2 in the appendix illustration (pp.16-17). No operational basis is given, and p.13 says max-trip tests were not listed because no clear differences were found.
records.benefit_reported_as: Total travel time and algorithm performance; Table 5 reports travel-time sensitivity to vehicle counts. The paper does not isolate a single-trip baseline (pp.1,12-14).
records.fixed_cost_billing_unit: NONE. Objective (1) contains travel times only (p.4).

records.paper: Fermín Cueto, P.; Gjeroska, I.; Solà Vilalta, A.; Anjos, M. F. (2021), A solution approach for multi-trip vehicle routing problems with time windows, fleet sizing, and depot location, Networks 78:503-522
records.multitrip_evidence: p.504 defines a trip as one physical vehicle leaving the depot, visiting customers, and returning, and explicitly permits multiple trips. p.506 orders consecutive trips of the same vehicle; p.515 describes packing routes into vehicle trips.
records.fleet_size_given_or_endogenous: TWO-STAGE. Fleet size is endogenously estimated at the strategic stage, then fixed as the daily operational upper bound (pp.510-513).
records.how_total_derived: Simulate n=50 busy-demand realizations using Bernoulli customer activation, Poisson(9.95) active demand, and calibrated beta; solve a multi-trip VRP for each realization; set each depot's final fleet to the 95th percentile of the 50 vehicle requirements (pp.509-510).
records.total_shrinks_or_fixed: The strategic fleet is designed with multi-trip-aware VRPs and then held constant over daily operations. Daily usage may be lower; shortages are met with rentals. Table 2 gives 12/14/16/18 vehicles for P75/P95/Max/Max+10% criteria (pp.511,513).
records.max_trips_per_vehicle: No numerical trip-count cap. Potential trip set R is bounded in practice by depot hours 06:00-17:00, customer windows 08:00-16:00, and consecutive-trip timing (pp.504,506,513,515).
records.benefit_reported_as: Fleet requirement, fixed fleet cost, peak-day rental count and cost, total vehicle cost, and utilization risk (pp.510-513); no isolated single-trip baseline.
records.fixed_cost_billing_unit: Per assigned physical vehicle. Vehicle lease/purchase, insurance, and driver wages are vehicle fixed costs (p.506); daily fleet cost is fixed regardless of daily utilization (p.513). Extra rentals are per vehicle-day at $90/day (p.511).

records.paper: Wang, L.; Ding, Y.; Chen, Z.; Su, Z.; Zhuang, Y. (2024), Heuristic Algorithms for Heterogeneous and Multi-Trip Electric Vehicle Routing Problem with Pickup and Delivery, World Electric Vehicle Journal 15:69
records.multitrip_evidence: p.1 explicitly models multiple trips per vehicle per day in a 06:00-24:00 delivery window. pp.5-6 index x by vehicle type k, physical vehicle g, and trip u; timing constraint (7) orders consecutive trips of the same g.
records.fleet_size_given_or_endogenous: GIVEN AVAILABILITY. Each of two EV types has Max_Vehicle_Cnt=500 (Table 2, p.13); trips and vehicle assignments are optimized within that availability.
records.how_total_derived: The paper directly gives 500 available vehicles per type and supplies no relation to demand, capacity, time windows, or daily horizon (p.13).
records.total_shrinks_or_fixed: Availability remains 500 per type; no single-trip versus multi-trip fleet-total comparison is reported (pp.5-6,13).
records.max_trips_per_vehicle: No numeric value is given for the cardinality of H^{kg}. The 06:00-24:00 horizon, time windows, and consecutive-trip timing limit realized trips (pp.1,5-6).
records.benefit_reported_as: Total cost and its travel, waiting, charging, and vehicle-cost components; the motivation says multi-trip can reduce fleet size, but experiments do not isolate that causal effect (pp.1,17-21).
records.fixed_cost_billing_unit: PER ACTIVE TRIP, not per physical vehicle. Equation (1) sums F^k times the depot-departure variable for every trip u, and the text says F^k is added when a type-k vehicle on trip u departs the depot (p.6).

records.paper: Zhao, J.; Poon, M.; Tan, V. Y. F.; Zhang, Z. (2024), A hybrid genetic search and dynamic programming-based split algorithm for the multi-trip time-dependent vehicle routing problem, European Journal of Operational Research 317:921-935
records.multitrip_evidence: p.922 states that every physical vehicle can undertake multiple depot-customer-depot trips within [E,L]. p.923 indexes x by physical vehicle k and trip r and defines z_k for whether physical vehicle k is used.
records.fleet_size_given_or_endogenous: AVAILABLE SET GIVEN; ACTUAL USED FLEET ENDOGENOUS. K={1,...,K} is available, while z_k and N_veh determine usage (pp.922-923).
records.how_total_derived: No external or demand/capacity formula for available K is reported. The model minimizes trip duration plus P times the number of used physical vehicles (p.923).
records.total_shrinks_or_fixed: The availability ceiling is held fixed and actual used vehicles decline. Table 6 shows cases where N_veh falls from 3 to 1 as P rises while N_trip remains 3; the text explains reuse of existing vehicles (pp.932-934).
records.max_trips_per_vehicle: No numeric cap. R={1,...,R} is defined for some sufficiently large integer R; [E,L], capacity, maximum trip distance D, and timing determine realized trips (pp.922-923).
records.benefit_reported_as: Total cost, used physical vehicles N_veh, total trips N_trip, and the trade-off between vehicle fixed cost and reuse (pp.932-934).
records.fixed_cost_billing_unit: PER USED PHYSICAL VEHICLE k: objective (1) contains P times sum_k z_k (p.923).

records.paper: Cavecchia, M.; Alves de Queiroz, T.; Lancellotti, R.; Zucchi, G.; Iori, M. (2025), A Real-World Multi-Depot, Multi-Period, and Multi-Trip Vehicle Routing Problem with Time Windows, ICORES 2025:112-122
records.multitrip_evidence: p.112 says a physical vehicle performs multiple trips in a period and returns to its depot. pp.114-116 define a vehicle route as one or more trips, add loading time Delta between consecutive trips, and assign/sequence trips on vehicle k.
records.fleet_size_given_or_endogenous: CANDIDATE SET GIVEN; ACTUAL USED FLEET ENDOGENOUS. K_v indexes candidate vehicles, y_kv selects physical vehicles, and the constructive method creates a new vehicle only when no used vehicle can accept a trip (pp.114-116).
records.how_total_derived: No formula derives the candidate total from demand/capacity/time. Actual required physical vehicles are an optimized output and are reported by depot and type in Table 3 (pp.119-120).
records.total_shrinks_or_fixed: No ex-ante proportional shrink. Generated trips are packed into physical vehicles while minimizing usage cost; the resulting used fleet is reported (pp.116,119-120).
records.max_trips_per_vehicle: No numerical cap. A route may contain one or more trips and is limited by per-period working hours T, customer time windows, and loading/unloading time Delta between trips (pp.114-116).
records.benefit_reported_as: Total vehicle-usage cost and number of physical vehicles used, with Table 3 reporting used vehicles by depot and type (pp.115-116,119-120). No isolated single-trip baseline.
records.fixed_cost_billing_unit: A_v is incurred once when a physical vehicle is used at least once across all periods; B_v is incurred when that vehicle is used for a route in a period. A route may contain multiple trips (p.115).

common_finding: True multi-trip papers most often expose the physical fleet requirement or used-vehicle count and, when fixed cost is charged per physical vehicle, translate reuse into fleet-cost savings. Algorithm benchmark papers often report travel time and feasibility instead of a causal multi-trip saving.
